title: Leaving work
hook: a clear end to the workday: in Genesis, God looks back, calls it very good, and ends the work
tomorrow: can sweeping a room turn it into gold?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: at my desk. The Buddha washed the monk nobody tended. Today, the desk gets a closing time.
screen: `AT MY DESK.` → `THE DESK GETS A CLOSING TIME.`

segments.voice: The laptop is closed. Then the phone buzzes at eleven, and the workday quietly starts again. Genesis tells how a stretch of work ends. After six days of making light and sea, plants, animals and people, God looks at it all: "And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good." Then the text slows down: "And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made."
screen: `THE PHONE BUZZES AT ELEVEN.` → `SIX DAYS OF MAKING.` → `GOD ENDED HIS WORK.`

segments.voice: Notice the order. First, a look back. All through the chapter the text pauses to say what's made is good, and at the end, very good. Then, an ending on purpose. The work doesn't fizzle out at midnight; it's ended. And the word good comes before the word rested. The rest isn't a collapse at the end of the week. It follows a verdict. Jews built a whole day on that ending. The commandments in Exodus point straight back to this chapter: "Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work," and the seventh is the sabbath, for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and rested. That's Shabbat, the Jewish day of rest, which begins at sundown on Friday. Christians hear the same chapter behind their own day of rest. The teaching for a workday is the shape of it: look at what you did, call it good, or good enough, and end it on purpose. Not because the list is empty. Lists are never empty. Because the ending is part of the work. You can hear it in the text's rhythm: made, saw, good, ended, rested.
screen: `FIRST A LOOK BACK: VERY GOOD.` · `THEN AN ENDING, ON PURPOSE.` · `SIX DAYS OF WORK, THEN SHABBAT.` · `THE ENDING IS PART OF THE WORK.` · then, large: `DONE.`

segments.voice: Put both hands flat on a table or desk and feel its surface under your palms. Walk back through today's work, one piece at a time, and say quietly at the end of each: good. Then lift your hands off the table, slowly, and let them rest in your lap.
Leaving work: a clear end to the workday, looked back on and set down on purpose, the way Genesis ends the six days.
Hold onto this: done, seen and called good and set down for today. The workday's over.
